quest.title: Where Honed Blades Clash
quest.description: A fashion festival is being held in Fontaine. You and Paimon decide to check it out for yourselves...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x29525, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine: Quartier Lyonnais

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Fashion Week is coming up! My husband promised to get me a replica of the most eye-catching outfit from the show.

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Oh, I say! As expected of a high-flying merchant! How generous of him!

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Well, what a coincidence, though — my husband promised me precisely the same thing!

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Oh dear! Whatever are we going to do, then, if we fall in love with the same dress?

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Well, let's leave our gentlemen to figure that one out for themselves, shall we?
...Excuse me! Coming through, coming through!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: ...Chiori, your... Your shipment's here. I know it's quite late, so I'm... really... really sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Deep breaths, Kirara — then start again.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Huh? And you're with customers as well? Oh geez... I've really kept everyone waiting. I'm so sorry, this is all my fault.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: #These two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon. With how well-traveled you are, you've probably heard of them already.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And this is Kirara, star courier of Komaniya Express. She's a nekomata, in case you were wondering about the tails.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Pleased to make your acquaintance, and sorry you had to see me like this! I know I'm late, but if an opportunity arises in the future, I still hope you'll choose the Komaniya Express!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, so Kirara's the courier you were talking about!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: #Oh hey, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Fancy seeing you here in Fontaine! It's been a while.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Wait a second... This is the second time that you've seen me flub a delivery job now, isn't it... You somehow always happen to catch me off my game, huh...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: So what was the hold up? Sailing delays? Bad weather?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Huh? No, nothing like that... I just ran into a bit of trouble, that's all.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Bandits, then? Or Treasure Hoarders? Huh, a few run ins on the road aren't usually enough to give you any trouble...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Uh... Well, I didn't run into anyone, exactly. I just got a little lost...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Keeping you honest as always, I see.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Alright, alright... I was stopped by a group of bandits as soon as I entered Fontaine.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: They were a little different from the ones I usually run into. I could hear them mumbling about the Komaniya Express. It was obvious they were looking for someone with two tails...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? So it was a targeted hit?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Uh... I got the sense that they were actually targeting Chiori's goods.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: My fabric shipment?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Yeah, they said that I could go as long as I left the goods with them. Otherwise, they'd stuff me into my delivery box and toss me into the sea to drown...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Are you okay, Kirara?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I'm good, I'm good! I'm still a youkai, after all. I turned them over to the Gardes. It just took me a while to round them all up...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, it's not completely out of the ordinary for one of your deliveries to get intercepted. But it still doesn't make sense how you knew it was my goods they were after. You've got other deliveries to make in Fontaine, don't you?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Is there something else that you're keeping from me?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Huh!? Um, well...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm... Perhaps I need to reconsider how many stars to give you in my review...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Ah! You always know how to get me, Chiori! Alright, I'll talk, I'll talk...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: So... I kinda wanted to know why anyone would order a hit on me, so I spent a bit of time investigating.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: One of the bandits had a loose tongue, which saved me some time. He said that a certain person had commissioned them to intercept Chioriya Boutique's delivery.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: And who might this person be?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Uh, Chiori, why don't we just let this one go. I mean, I didn't really get injured, and you've still got Fashion Week to worry about...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I appreciate your kindness, Kirara, but if I don't teach this person a lesson, I doubt they'll stop here.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Anyone that dares to mess with one of my friends deserves a stern talking to and then some.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: ...Alright. The guy said that the commissioner was someone by the name of "Uther."

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Uther... Now, that name rings a bell, wouldn't you say, Kirara?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Well, that's exactly why I didn't want to bring it up to you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, so you both know this Uther guy?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Through Chiori's complaints about him, sure. He's a fellow fashion designer who's made it his goal in life to make hers as miserable as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So is he like... a business rival?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: A "rival" is what you call someone who fights you fair and square.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Uther, however, just has it out for me as a designer. He's publicly disparaged my design choices, my use of materials — he's practically tried every trick in the book to ruin my good name.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I've already warned him before to compete with me fair and square, but I guess he prefers playing dirty. Well, I'm more than happy to oblige...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Wait, Chiori, where are you going?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: To teach someone a lesson. You must be tired after your long journey — why don't you rest in my shop for a little while before heading back?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Chiori... Wait!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaand... She's gone.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Oh no... What should we do...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You seem concerned... Should we be worried about Chiori?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Well, she's always been the type of person to face things head-on. But, with her fiery temper... I'm just worried whatever she's about to do will fuel negative publicity about her right before the start of Fashion Week.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, could you go after her and check out the situation for me? As a formal employee of the Komaniya Express, it wouldn't be appropriate for me to get involved.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We'll take good care of Chiori.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Uh, well, to be honest... I'm more worried about that Uther guy's safety...

choices.text: How about a game of Genius Invokation TCG?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Ahahaha... Maybe next time! Considering how late this delivery is, I'm not sure this is the time to play cards. Plus, I know this shipment is really important to Chiori, so I should probably make sure everything's in order...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Any chance you're on the clock, Officer?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Nothing good ever comes out of you addressing me like that.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Oh? And who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Ah, so you came, too.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: #Ah, allow me to introduce you. These two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon. This officer over here is Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The... The Special Security and Surveillance Patrol? You mean that organization where everyone carries a musket?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Well, I wouldn't say everyone on the Patrol uses a musket. I just happen to have formed a platoon made up mostly of musketeers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Chiori, Paimon didn't know you went so far back with such a cool person!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It's nothing. In my line of work, it's not uncommon to run into some trouble every now and then, and she's helped me get out of a few sticky situations.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: In return, I've helped her take care of some things that you could say aren't exactly in her purview as the captain of the Special Patrol... and that's how we got to know each other.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's nice to meet you both. I have to say, your reputation precedes you.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Oh? And I see the Traveler and Paimon are here too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chevreuse! We meet again!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Well, things have been fine on my end. We were able to bring in a large number of recruits thanks to that film we made.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I suppose the trade off is that I'm now constantly getting stopped for autographs while out on patrol — not ideal if you ask me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, well, you were one of the leading roles, after all!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: So, did something happen?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Indeed it did. I'll need you to come with me.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...I only ever hear that phrase from you. Usually, I'm the one asking people to do that.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, are you coming?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Not before I know what you're planning.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Have I ever made a bad call?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The better question is, have you ever made one that didn't violate proper procedure?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Okay, a man hired a group of bandits to mug my friend. I'm about to go teach him a lesson.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Are you sure this is something you should be telling the captain of the Special Patrol? It's getting hard to tell whether you're here to report a case or turn yourself in for one.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Neither. I'm requesting personal supervision from said captain so I don't do anything too out of line.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Are you planning to?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Not if I can help it.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Alright, where is this person?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: This should be the place. You all wait here. I'll go have a chat with him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Chevreuse, Paimon gets the sense that you two are actually pretty close.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's just as Chiori said — we got to know each other pretty well in our lines of work... You could call it a "you scratch my back, and I'll scratch yours" sort of situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does Chiori often need your help?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Eh, I'd say it's mutual. The Special Patrol needs her help quite often as well. We've got tough problems of our own — getting people to talk, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The uniform, the musket, they're intimidating. Most people clam up the minute they see us, lips sealed so tight, getting them to talk almost feels like trying to break into the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: But put them in a clothing boutique, and they suddenly start gushing faster than the waters at the Fountain of Lucine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Is it because they're trying to show off or something?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yep. People are vain creatures — they can't help but want to talk up new developments in their lives, or show off how much they know about other people. And nothing brings out that sort of vanity quite like fashion.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: As a result, Chiori often picks up on all kinds of information in her shop. Most of her customers are members of the upper class, which means they're pretty much up to the gills in wealth and intel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You scratch my back, and I'll scratch yours... Paimon gets it now.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Exactly. I'm also here to ensure Chiori's safety. Those who make trouble for her also tend to be rich and powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And in some very rare cases... I'm forced to protect other people from Chiori herself.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: So, who got on her case this time? It's been a while since I last saw her that angry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so this is what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Uther, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've heard of him?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He's made trouble for Chiori's several times already. He's fond of pretty much every dirty trick in the book. I heard that even the Maison Gardiennage issued him a warning due to his behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...So, he's back at it, huh? His funeral, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, what's this about a funeral all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I just meant that Uther's done for. Now, bring it in, you two. Get right up close...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Ah, sure... But why?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Because this is probably going to turn into one of those "very rare cases" I just talked about...

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: Arghhhhh!

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: Wh—What are you doing? Stay away from me!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Has anyone ever taught you... the definition of stupidity?

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Stupidity... is doing the same meaningless thing over and over again.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It appears you've forgotten what I told you before, so allow me to refresh your memory — lay off the dirty tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, and if you dare lay your hands on my friend again, you can expect a far less pleasant landing next time.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Ahem, Chiori...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: Ah, Officer! An assault's in progress! Please, Officer, you've got to do something!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Of course. I'll do my utmost to investigate the situation. Unfortunately, I was chatting with this Traveler and seem to have missed what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not to worry, though. If you'd allow me to search the scene, I'm sure I'll be able to collect some useful evidence. You don't mind, do you? There's nothing in there that would implicate you in any illegal activity, I would hope...

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: I... Argh, forget it, it wasn't that big of a deal...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Ms. Chiori, I must also ask you to refrain from engaging in such disorderly conduct in the future, especially out in the open like this.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Ah, apologies, Officer. I guess you could say I'm just used to tossing out any trash I come across on the street.

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Is there anything else either of you have to say for yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: That's all from me. I sincerely hope that today's events will never happen again.

dialogues.speaker: Uther
dialogues.text: ...We'll see about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, that scared the heck out of Paimon! How did he just go... flying out like that?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You're too kind.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Now's not the time to be accepting compliments. What happened to not doing anything too out of line?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Not if I could help it is what I said — and I think I kept to that.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I started with a verbal warning, but he displayed neither shame nor remorse. If anything, he kept running his mouth with insults and threats.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Insults and threats so bad that he deserved to be tossed out like a sack of trash?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Believe it or not, they were that bad. He deserved to get knocked down a peg. It's the only way to get him to stop.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...You could have reported him to the Gardes.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oh, I will, but it'll take some time for them to gather evidence, and he'd deny that he ever had anything to do with those bandits.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I don't want anything else to happen during Fontaine Fashion Week. On top of that, if Kirara's going to continue delivering goods for me, the least I can do is guarantee her safety.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Ah, that reminds me — there's another favor I'd like to ask of you today.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: What a shame. I believe you've already used up your favor quota for the day.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Have I? Well, it's a good thing I was planning on taking an advance on tomorrow's quota then.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...Don't you think you're maxed out on advances already?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I always pay you back in information, don't I?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: It's just like you said — you scratch my back, and I scratch yours.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: We're back.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: You were gone for an awfully long time! P—Please tell me nothing bad happened...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: There's nothing to worry about. All you need to know is that you'll never have to worry about someone in Fontaine messing with your deliveries again.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Sorry, Chiori... I didn't mean to cause you so much trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? You didn't do anything wrong. Those greedy bandits are to blame... along with a certain someone who doesn't know when to lay off the petty tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The next time you need to leave the city, call the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. They'll escort you half of the way, and the Spina di Rosula can take the second half...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: With that sort of escort, the next time you make a delivery, those Treasure Hoarders won't go anywhere near your goods... unless, of course, it's to offer to carry them for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... Good one, Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I'm being serious. You know me — if I bring something up, you can assume it's already a done deal. You're going back to Inazuma tomorrow, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Wait, you don't mean—

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I've already spoken to the Captain of the Special Patrol. As discussed, the Patrol's going to take a small detour during their daily training tomorrow. As for Navia... I'll give her a heads-up in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: There's really no need! I'm just a simple courier! I don't need to be surrounded by a bunch of armed guards... or ones with sunglasses for that matter. Don't you think this is a bit much?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well, you certainly shouldn't count on such a procession for every trip you make to Fontaine. It's just a one-off thing... for my own peace of mind.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It'll also show those guys what'll happen to those who dare to mess with my friends.

choices.text: Since she's already talked to the Patrol...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Well, if you think it's a good idea, Traveler, then I guess it's fine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, with the bad guys out of the way and your goods safely delivered, everything should be good to go for Fontaine Fashion Week, right?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I believe so. I'll try to churn out a few more outfits over the next few days. I've heard a lot of suppliers will be participating this year.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's gonna take a guess and say suppliers are super important...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But of course. They supply us designers with funding, equipment, factory access... You have to work with them if you want to become a truly renowned fashion house.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: That's also why this year's Fashion Week is so important to me.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: But isn't your brand already really famous, Chiori? Your clothes are so pretty and so nice to wear... I can't help but brag about them to my customers whenever I get the chance.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Even so, I would imagine there are still people who've never heard of the "Chioriya" brand, yes?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Weeeeelll... I mean, with the amount of places that I deliver to, it's only natural that some people from other nations haven't heard of it.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Then it's still not famous enough. My goal is to make the Chioriya brand renowned throughout all of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All of it!? Your business would have to get pretty huge, then!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Wait, would that mean I could just go to any Chioriya branch on the continent to get my clothes fixed? It has been pretty inconvenient, having to come to Fontaine every time I need to get them patched up...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alternatively, of course, you could just be a bit more careful with them... They're already about as durable as I can make them.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Hehe... okay I'll admit, they do get snagged on branches pretty often, but I can't help it! It's hard to be careful about that sort of thing when you're trying to take a nice nap in a tree...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if that's your dream, Chiori, then we should do our best to make it a reality! Is there anything we can do to help out with Fashion Week?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm... I'm sure I could think of something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, what is it? What is it?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Why don't you come to my shop tomorrow and model for me? Simply put, you'll serve as my living mannequins.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So we get to try on some of your clothes? Got it!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Seeing them off the rack will also give me the chance to make some small adjustments to the stitching and silhouette of the designs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds easy enough!

choices.text: Do you need us for the runway, too?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No need. We've already booked the models for that.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If you like them, though, feel free to visit the boutique and see if anything catches your eye. I'll even give you a special discount.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, sounds great! Paimon was just starting to get curious about all of this design stuff.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: #Then we have a deal. You'll model some formal wear, {NICKNAME}, and... I dunno, Paimon here will show off some kids' designs. I'll see you both tomorrow then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, sounds goo— Wait... Kids clothes? Paimon told you already. She's not a little kid!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Most of the clothes you see during Fashion Week are meant to showcase the designer's vision. They're not exactly suitable for ready-to-wear use.

choices.text: Just think of it as a "you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours" type of situation...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yes, well put.

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Is... Is this really okay?
I told you I could do it using the leftover funds from the original deposit. Don't tell me you're afraid that I cheaped out on the dress?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: No, not at all! I have only the fullest faith in your work, Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: I'm just in shock, that's all. It's always been my dream to wear a Chioriya Boutique dress for my wedding... I really thought the chance had passed me by...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, is that lady the owner of Chioriya Boutique? We've never seen her before!

choices.text: Her work probably keeps her very busy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, isn't that Chiori? She's actually at her shop today!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps it's because of "Fontaine Fashion Week"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, you've got a point there! Well, once she's done with her customer, we can go and ask her!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I'm a woman of my word — If I say I can do something, then it will be done. The first rule of business is to always keep your promises.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Now, remember to not fold the gown, or store it under direct sunlight. I'd recommend only taking it out on the day of your wedding, but from the look on your face... I can tell that may be a little difficult for you.

response.speaker: Laetitia
response.text: I—I'll try my best! Hehe... Once he sees me in this, his jaw is gonna drop straight to the floor!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...Are you here to check out the offerings?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sure are! Paimon's Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. You're Ms. Chiori, the owner of this boutique, right?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: That's right. Navia's told me about you — glad to make your acquaintance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've heard a lot about you, too! "Chioriya Boutique" is super famous in Fontaine!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, I appreciate the recognition. Is there anything you're looking for exactly? We're out of kids' clothes right now, I am afraid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chiori! You're actually at your shop today!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Is that really so shocking? It is mine, after all.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Anything you're looking for today? A custom design, or perhaps some ready-to-wear outfits for kids?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon's not a kid!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We actually wanted to ask about "Fontaine Fashion Week"...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Ah, that. Well, if news of the event has reached your ears, I suppose the Fontaine Apparel Association's advertising efforts have paid off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are there any fun and popular activities that we can take part in?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm... Fashion Week isn't what I'd call "fun," but it certainly always attracts a crowd. It's a fashion extravaganza that only takes place once a year, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Will you be showing off some of your designs, too?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Of course. All designers at the Court of Fontaine use the week to advertise their brand. If you're lucky, you could even land a large amount of orders as soon as the main show ends.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Come to think of it, it was also at a previous Fashion Week that our label first took off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... aren't you pretty much an established name now? People will still buy your clothes even if you don't participate this year, right?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: That's not quite how it works. While many people buy clothes for fit and style, the fashion industry also strongly values a label's artistic vision and creative direction.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Why would anyone patronize a label that hasn't even bothered to put out any new designs for the year?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: In the end, "fashion" is just a representation of the spirit of the times. People support your brand because they support the vision it represents.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh okay... so maybe fashion's more complicated than Paimon thought...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All that complicated stuff aside, you're saying we'll be able to see new Chioriya designs at the show?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Absolutely. The designs have already been finalized — I'm just waiting for the fabrics to arrive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Are you using materials you can't get in Fontaine?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, I still have a certain partiality to Inazuma-made fabrics. The textures are pleasant to the touch, and their familiarity gives me a sense of security.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon gets it. It's that feeling of home!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Something like that, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're a long way from Inazuma, though! Aren't you concerned that your shipment might get lost or stolen on the way?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No need to worry. I've already taken steps to ensure that it will arrive safely — I've entrusted the job to Komaniya Express's most reliable courier.

choices.text: Well, Eloffe is usually the one staffing the shop...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I told you I could do it using the leftover funds from the original deposit. Don't tell me you're afraid that I cheaped out on the dress?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Anyway, please look after Chiori for me.

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: The much-anticipated Fontaine Fashion Week has begun!

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: Many renowned designers have gathered for this event. Their meticulously crafted, brand-new works will be on display during the final show.

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: Let the light of fashion shine upon the City of the Arts!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like there's another event going on at the Court of Fontaine! Look at that — roadside signs as far as the eye can see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see what they're for... "Fontaine Fashion Week"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, why don't we go check out some of the shops? Maybe we can pick up some cool new clothes!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Just promise you'll start trying to keep yourself out of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well, when trouble stops coming my way, I'll be sure to get on that.

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: ...It's Fashion Week right now...
